text:
maria: Heads-up — eviction ripple in ap-southeast1 after last night's mixed-node rollout. Lots of small 24GB pods getting scheduled onto 48GB machines, then preempted when rack balancing runs. Seeing cross-AZ spill to us-west2.

jon: Any error logs? Pod events?

maria: Quick sample:```
kubectl get pods -n ml-serving -o wide | grep Evicted
model-a-abcde   0/1 Evicted   24h   10.0.1.34   ap-southeast1a
model-b-fghij   0/1 Evicted   23h   10.0.2.90   ap-southeast1b
```
Pod events show: "Pod evicted: Insufficient gpu.memory" even though node shows free GPU memory in metrics.

lee: Scheduler logs look noisy: `fits: Insufficient gpu.memory` and later `assume/predicate passed` for same node. Feels like the scheduler treats GPU flavors as interchangeable but kubelet/container-runtime reports different usable memory per GPU.

anika: :thinking: We rolled a new instance class (gpu-x48) into the ASG without tagging labels. No gpu.memclass label, so the scheduler is happily packing small 24GB workload onto large nodes. When our binpacker runs or the autoscaler evicts to rebalance, pods get preempted due to per-GPU allocation mismatch.

ryan: We hit a similar edge in eu-west with v2 vs v1 GPUs. Short-term mitigation: throttle the rollout and add a nodeSelector for legacy 24GB pools on critical workloads. Longer-term: scheduler awareness of gpu.memory class.

ops: :money_with_wings: Also note cross-AZ spill increases egress/cost. If pods bounce between regions it adds bandwidth + SLO risk.

sre-bot: Alert: evictions > 200 in ap-southeast1 between 1762300000 and 1762340000. See grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/evictions/evict-overview?orgId=1

lee: Quick stopgap: taint the 48GB nodes with `gpu.memclass=large:PreferNoSchedule` so the scheduler will avoid placing 24GB-only pods there unless tolerated. Then add toleration for workloads that explicitly want 48GB.

maria: We already have a handful of customers pinned to large nodes but autoscaler joining without labels caused the mix. I cordoned the new ASG for now.

anika: Action plan: 1) rollback ASG join in ap-southeast1 (maria done) 2) add cloud-init script to set `gpu.memclass` label on boot for each image/instance-type 3) ship kube-scheduler plugin config to prefer same memclass packing 4) migration job to drain non-critical pods and force schedule onto matching pools. I'll open a PR and a rollback runbook.

jon: For migration we can do a low-priority eviction job: `kubectl -n ml-serving delete pod -l evictable=true --grace-period=30` to shift traffic. I'll prepare a safe job that respects PodDisruptionBudgets.

ops: I'll create a ticket for cost tracking + temporarily pause cluster autoscaler for the affected zone.

maria: Thanks team. For now I've paused the rollout and cordoned the ASG. Next steps: schedule a small canary of labeled nodes, land the kube-scheduler change behind a feature flag, then gradual rollout. Assigning: @anika (labeling + scheduler PR), @jon (migration job), @ops (cost ticket + autoscaler pause). :thumbsup:

ryan: Heads-up: once fixed let's run an eval on packing efficiency; mixing mem classes improved utilization but needs smarter packing to avoid churn.

maria: Agreed. We'll aim for a scheduler change that looks at `gpu.memclass` and `gpu.memory` when scoring.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-143 (ap-southeast1 eviction wave).
